population.note: FICTIONAL. About 23.2% of US adults (≈61M of ≈265M) say they are currently on an incretin drug, 29% ever. Age-weighted check: 0.20×12 + 0.33×23 + 0.24×35 + 0.23×21 ≈ 23.2. Cycling arithmetic: ever 29 − current 23 = 6 pp used and off now. Current users who stopped at least once before restarting ≈ 8.5 pp, and the off-now who had already cycled once ≈ 1.5 pp, so (8.5 + 1.5) / 29 ≈ 34% of ever-users have stopped and restarted. That fits the 2026 figures: one-year persistence of about a third, and 36–47% of stoppers restarting. Most of the 2026 cohort stopped and many came back. About 10 pp of the ever-users started within the last 12 months and have not yet had time to stop. 'Currently on' is self-reported and counts people on dose holidays of under a month, which inflates it compared with continuous-fill measures. One-year persistence on continuous fills has risen to about 42%, helped by cheaper pills and no injection. Never-users: 71% of adults. Among adults with obesity in the bottom income third, about 1 in 5 are on a drug, against about 1 in 2 in the top third. Pediatric: ≈0.6% of under-18s (≈440k), roughly 3% of children with obesity, up from 0.6% in 2026; mostly ages 12+, with prescribing still skewed to upper-income families. The income split is a simulation estimate, not published data.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the GLP-1 Bridge pilot ran to Dec 2027 and passed, as already planned, into the CMS Part D obesity model, keeping $245/month to the plan and a $50 copay. Plans can choose whether to take part, and about 70% of Part D enrollees are in plans that do. About 2.5M beneficiaries fill under an obesity indication: 2.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.4B a year in gross federal spend. That is well above the ≈$3.9B/yr average implied by CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–2034 score, and the overrun is a live budget story. Another ≈7.9M Medicare users fill under diabetes or cardiovascular codes, as before. Medicaid: about 30 states cover obesity at the $245 reference rate, ≈6.1M users. Approximate payer mix of the ≈61M users: cash 40% (24.4M), commercial 30% (18.3M), Medicare 17% (10.4M), Medicaid 10% (6.1M), gray/import 3% (1.8M).
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 60+ brands at $6–40/month. Canada: generic semaglutide at about CAD 70–100/month; Health Canada limited bulk export after US cross-border buying in 2027. Brazil, Mexico and much of Southeast Asia now have generics. Cost-plus generic injectable semaglutide is sold in about 160 countries. No US generic semaglutide or tirzepatide; exclusivity runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels sell Foundayo at $149 for all doses. The Wegovy pill costs $199–249 depending on dose, after the tariff-exemption deal. Injectable Wegovy and Zepbound sell for $249–299 cash. Retatrutide (approved Aug 2028) launched through LillyDirect at $349 and on a $1,299 list price. Wegovy's $1,349 list price still exists on paper. Employer coverage for weight management fell from 60% to 44% (Business Group on Health, 2028). Most remaining plans limit coverage to type 2 diabetes, established cardiovascular disease, obstructive sleep apnea and, since May 2028, the dementia-risk label in diabetes. Pure-BMI coverage survives mainly at large tech, finance and public-sector employers. Daily orals made up about 62% of new starts in 2028 and roughly half of current users. The FDA finalised the 503B bulks exclusion in 2027. Tariffs and import alerts on Chinese peptide API hit compounders, keeping the gray market contained at about 3% of users, mostly Canadian or Mexican generics carried across the border.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg and 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Aug 2028)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction in risk of dementia / cognitive decline in adults 50+ with type 2 diabetes (semaglutide, May 2028; approved with a confirmatory-trial requirement)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'brain health' use by non-diabetic adults 50–64 following the dementia label, mostly cash-pay oral
alcohol reduction: guideline-endorsed as an option in AUD with obesity, still not an FDA indication
weekend or 'event' dose holidays on short half-life orforglipron
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral-parity driver is met by an existing product in a new form. A higher-dose Wegovy pill (50 mg) was approved as a supplemental application in Jun 2027, after a head-to-head trial found it non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (≈16–17% vs ≈16%). The pill matches semaglutide injections but not tirzepatide (≈21%) or retatrutide. Foundayo (≈12%) is the cheaper, domestically made pill. CagriSema was approved Jan 2027 after the late-2026 review, with modest uptake because it failed non-inferiority against tirzepatide. Retatrutide's BLA was filed Feb 2027 and approved Aug 2028 (more than 12 months after filing). It carries a dysesthesia warning, and use is concentrated in BMI≥35. Amycretin and survodutide remain in phase 3 with no US approval; survodutide filed in mid-2028. MariTide is still in development. Dementia: the 2025 EVOKE trials in established Alzheimer's failed. The 2028 label rests on a narrower population, adults with diabetes and no dementia, using a prespecified cognitive-outcome endpoint plus pooled CVOT data. Neurologists dispute how large the effect is. Global incretin market ≈$118B in 2028: volume growth offset by falling price per patient.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of discontinuation. Daily orals with gradual titration report slightly lower early dropout.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; not recommended in severe gastroparesis.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Raised with rapid weight loss; more cases seen with retatrutide's larger losses.
Long-term data still do not confirm causation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; multidistrict litigation continues, no verdicts.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈25–30% of weight lost is lean mass. Concern focuses on adults 65+, whose use doubled. Bone-density questions remain open.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None from regulators. Muscle adjuncts are still in trials; strength training is the de facto prescription.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort data still conflict; no new signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now surveyed but not trialled. In a 2028 national survey (fictional), 27% of current users reported 'muted enjoyment' at least weekly; 4 in 10 of them had cut their dose or taken holidays. No validated anhedonia scale has been used in a registration trial.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. FDA asked for patient-reported mood outcomes in some postmarketing studies; manufacturers describe dose individualisation.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Trial data still show most of the loss regained within a year. Real-world regain is smaller among people who move to a lower maintenance dose. Short holidays show little regain.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; supports chronic-therapy framing and maintenance dosing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Observational reports continue, especially in older and low-income users eating little.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; professional societies recommend nutrition screening.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of rigorous follow-up now exist. Still no data on decades-long adolescent use or on repeated cycling, which a third of ever-users have now done.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements on new approvals (Foundayo, CagriSema, retatrutide).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New reports slowed after the 503B exclusion. Counterfeit 'Canadian generic' pens are a smaller, ongoing problem.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised (2027); import alerts on unregistered peptide API.

food_and_beverage.state: About 33% of US households now include a user. Packaged snack and confectionery volume is down about 3–4% a year in 2027–28; sugary drinks down about 2%. Big Food has moved from 'adapting' to cutting: Mondelez-type portfolios are selling under-performing indulgence brands to private-equity buyers. Protein, fibre and 'small-format' lines grow but do not replace lost volume. Discount grocers in lower-income areas see little change. The decline is concentrated in suburban and affluent baskets.

alcohol.state: US spirits volume is down about 5% across 2027–28, wine down more. The heaviest-drinking 10% of customers are shrinking fastest. Bars report a 'Friday spike' from orforglipron users skipping doses before the weekend. Non-alcoholic and functional drinks are growing but on a small base.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Premium casual and tasting-portion menus are doing well in affluent zip codes. Value chains are holding up on lower-income customers who are mostly not on the drug. Average check per diner is up on premiumisation; food volume per cover is down.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking; Torrid has closed about a fifth of its stores. Premium athleisure and tailored fits for lean, muscular bodies are growing in metro markets. Mid-tier apparel holds steady.

fitness.state: Strength training is now a status habit. Boutique strength studios and 'GLP-1 companion' memberships at $150–300/month are growing fast in affluent suburbs. Budget gyms are steady.

insurance.state: Employers are retreating to diabetes, cardiac and cognitive codes. Insurers are adding 'step-to-oral' rules that require Foundayo before injectables. Pharmacy cost growth eased to about 8% as unit prices fell, but per-member weight-loss coverage keeps shrinking.

pharma.state: Lilly is the clear leader, treated by policy as a domestic champion thanks to US small-molecule manufacturing of orforglipron. Novo is under pressure: it is Danish, subject to tariffs, and holds the parity pill but pays in price concessions. US revenue per patient is down about 30% since 2026; volume roughly doubled. The market is still growing, but more slowly than 2026 forecasts.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A lean, visibly muscled body now reads as income plus time: pill, trainer, protein. A merely thin body reads as 'on it'. A heavy body increasingly reads as uninsured, rural or working shifts. About half of adults know someone on a drug, and the question has moved from 'are you on it?' to 'which one, and who pays?'
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use runs from 30% in the top income third to about 15.5% in the bottom third, and the gap is widest among people with obesity. The class divide shows locally. In Plano and Frisco, Texas, professional women aged 30–49 are among the most medicated groups in the country, and the local gyms are strength studios. Forty miles east, in Kaufman and Van Zandt counties, obesity rates have barely moved. Cash $149 pills narrowed the gap at the bottom but did not close it: $1,788 a year is still a choice against rent.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: In affluent households dinner is smaller, protein-forward and earlier. Big shared meals survive as occasions, often planned around a skipped dose. Church potlucks and family barbecues in lower-income areas look much as they did. The cultural split is visible in what is on the table.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles in big-city markets openly list medication ('on Foundayo, love lifting'). Some users report lower libido and emotional flatness. Couples therapists describe 'mismatched appetite' between a medicated and an unmedicated partner as a routine complaint.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a dial, not a trait. Being able to afford to turn it down is a marker of class. Choosing to turn it back up for a weekend is a marker of control.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL survey estimate: about 27% of current users report weekly muted enjoyment and about 11% call it significant. Dose reduction and holidays are standard advice from telehealth clinicians. Orforglipron's short half-life makes 1–3 day holidays effective. Semaglutide's week-long half-life makes them mostly placebo, and users know it.
interior_life.framing: A widely shared complaint that people manage like a hangover: 'the flatness'. In AUD clinics the same effect is the treatment. Since the dementia label, some older users and their families frame steadiness and reduced craving as 'brain protection'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Managers in sales and creative roles complain about 'flat' teams, without data. Some users report better focus and less afternoon snacking or drinking. Employers do not encourage use and many no longer pay for it. Workplace talk centres on holiday scheduling around presentations and conferences.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Music venues and festivals report lower bar revenue and earlier crowds. Weekend dose-skipping has created a recognisable 'Saturday self'. Stand-up comedy treats 'the flatness' as stock material. Some musicians say publicly they come off the drug to tour or record.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Lower desire is the most common complaint after GI effects in user forums. Couples schedule holidays around anniversaries and vacations. 'Mismatched appetite' is common in therapy.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measurable effect on turnout or mood. The politics are about price and class: the US–Canada price gap, tariffs on Novo, and employers dropping coverage are 2028 campaign material. Both parties claim the $149 pill.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access and pro-speed on approvals, with priority vouchers used for retatrutide's review. The FDA keeps up enforcement against compounders and counterfeit imports. No new federal obesity-drug programme was created this step.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate and no new subsidy. The Medicare Bridge pilot passed into the previously planned CMS Part D obesity model at the same $245 rate and $50 copay. Medicaid coverage is a state-by-state choice, with about 30 states taking part. The TrumpRx cash channel continues.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Access depends on diagnosis codes, not BMI alone. Prior authorisation now commonly requires a trial of Foundayo first. No adherence monitoring beyond refill-based persistence checks by PBMs.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Supply is now political. Section 232 tariffs on imported branded drugs (2027) exempt firms that commit to US manufacturing. Novo bought its exemption by expanding US fill-finish capacity and cutting Wegovy pill prices. Lilly's US-made orforglipron is presented as a strategic domestic medicine. Import alerts and tariffs on Chinese peptide API hit compounders. Canada restricted bulk export of generic semaglutide after US cross-border buying. The US price is about 5–20× the Indian price, and that gap is a campaign talking point.

events.event: Commerce Department imposes Section 232 tariffs on imported branded pharmaceuticals, exempting companies with US manufacturing commitments. Lilly's domestic orforglipron plants are cited as the model. Novo wins an exemption by expanding US capacity and cutting Wegovy pill cash prices. Import alerts follow on Chinese peptide API.
FDA approves high-dose Wegovy pill (50 mg) after a head-to-head trial shows it non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg. Pills pass 60% of new starts by early 2028.
Health Canada restricts bulk export of generic semaglutide after US pharmacies and border-state buyers drain supply in Windsor and Vancouver.

Business Group on Health survey: 44% of large employers cover weight management, down from 60%. Most remaining plans limit coverage to diabetes, cardiac and sleep-apnea codes and require a trial of Foundayo before injectables.
FDA approves semaglutide to reduce the risk of dementia in adults 50+ with type 2 diabetes, requiring a confirmatory trial. Neurologists point to the 2025 EVOKE failure in established Alzheimer's.
Gallup: 23% of US adults now on an incretin drug, up from 11% in 2026. Retatrutide approved the next month.

open_tensions: Coverage now follows diagnosis codes while use follows income. The dementia label lets people with diabetes and money claim 'brain protection', while uninsured people with obesity pay $149 cash or go without.
The Medicare obesity model's gross run-rate (≈$7.4B/yr) is nearly double CBO's averaged score with no new appropriation, and plans can still opt out.

Pill holidays have made reward blunting something users switch on and off. A third of ever-users have cycled, and no one knows what weekly on/off dosing does over a decade, least of all in the 440k minors now on the drug.

Supply is caught up in tariff politics. The best pill is Danish and tariff-exempt only by deal; the domestic champion's pill is weaker; Canada has closed its border supply. One trade dispute could reprice the market.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity runs to roughly 2031–32.
Medicare pays ~$245/month for covered obesity GLP-1 use with a ~$50 beneficiary copay.
Wegovy's $1,349 list price remains on the books, though almost nobody pays it.
The FDA's January 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands.
Indian generic semaglutide sells for tens of dollars a month (now ~$6–40), a visible fraction of any US price.

prose.headline: One in Four Americans Is On It, and Their Bodies Show What They Earn
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 nearly a quarter of American adults say they are taking an incretin drug, and most of the newcomers swallowed rather than injected. Doctors had long said the needle held people back. What actually removed it was a dose: a 50-milligram Wegovy pill that did as well as the weekly injection in a head-to-head trial, plus Lilly's Foundayo, a weaker pill that costs $149 a month at any dose on the TrumpRx portal. Weekly injectables still sit at the top end. Zepbound, CagriSema and, since August, retatrutide with its 28 percent average loss are for the very heavy and the well covered. The ordinary starter now takes a tablet.

Prices fell the way the government's deals said they would. They did not fall the way they fell abroad. In Delhi semaglutide costs less than a sandwich. In Ohio the cheapest branded pill costs $1,788 a year, the injections up to $299 a month, and the old list prices survive only as a reference point. No American generic is coming before the early 2030s. Canada made sure its own was not an option: after border pharmacies in Windsor were emptied in 2027, Ottawa restricted bulk exports.

Employers kept leaving. Fewer than half of large companies now pay for weight loss as such, and those that pay for anything pay for diagnoses: diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea, and since May a dementia-risk label for semaglutide in people over fifty with diabetes. That label is narrow and contested. It came three years after the Alzheimer's trials failed, and neurologists say so on cable news. Still, it changed what the drug means to a 58-year-old with a prediabetic A1c and a father who no longer recognises her. Medicare's obesity coverage outlived the pilot and moved into the planned Part D model at the same $245 rate and $50 copay. It costs roughly twice what the Congressional Budget Office pencilled in, and no one has voted on the difference.

The drugs are also tied up in trade policy now. Tariffs on imported branded medicines spared companies that build in America, so Lilly's Indianapolis-and-Virginia pill gets talked about like a national asset. Novo, which holds the better pill, paid for its exemption with plants and price cuts. Compounders lost their Chinese peptide supply and most of their customers.

What the street sees is class. In Frisco the strength studios have waiting lists, and a lean, visibly muscled body works as a credential, like good teeth. Being merely thin means you are on it. Being heavy increasingly means you work shifts, live out past the county line, or have done the arithmetic and chosen rent. Use runs about twice as high in the top income third as in the bottom. Snack makers are selling brands they built in the 1980s. Discount grocers in Kaufman County have noticed nothing.

The flatness is now a common, ordinary complaint. About a quarter of users say pleasure arrives muted. The standard fix is to take less, or to skip a day or two. Foundayo's short half-life makes the skip work, so Friday has become a pharmacological event. Bartenders know it, musicians time their tours to it, and couples plan anniversaries around it. In addiction clinics the same blunting is the treatment. Nobody has settled whether it is a bug or a feature. People have decided it is a setting.

A third of everyone who has ever started has stopped and come back at least once. Four hundred and forty thousand children are on these drugs, most of them in households that can afford the strength coach too. The trials run about six years. The children may take the drug for sixty.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Ocampo, 44, takes her Foundayo at 6:10 with black coffee standing at the counter in Mesquite. She doesn't take Saturday's, because her niece's quinceañera is Saturday and she wants to taste the tres leches. The orange bottle says $149. The dental group dropped weight coverage last January. The HR email called it 'focusing benefits on clinical conditions.'

At the front desk she checks in Dr. Patel's 9:00, a woman from Frisco with arms like a rowing coach. She is on the Wegovy pill, through her husband's bank plan, she volunteers, as if Denise asked. The 10:30 is Mr. Lyle from Terrell, who is heavy and out of breath and pays his cleaning in two installments.

At lunch she eats half a turkey wrap and puts the other half in the drawer for tomorrow. The girls in billing are talking about a Netflix comedian's bit about 'the flatness.' Denise laughs because it's funny and because it's true. She hasn't wanted to dance since March.

After work she drives her mother's Rybelsus to Balch Springs. Medicare covers it for her diabetes, and since spring the pharmacist has been calling it 'the memory one.' Her mother asks again whether Denise is eating enough. Denise says yes. Her mother tells her she looks like a lady from television, and doesn't mean it as a compliment.

On the way home a billboard on I-30 shows a pill bottle on a flag: MADE HERE. PRICED FOR YOU. She does the math on $149 against the electric bill. Then she sets an alarm to not take Saturday's.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Retatrutide's BLA was filed Feb 2027 and approved Aug 2028 (more than 12 months after filing).
least_plausible_claims.why: Starting world says the BLA is planned ~Q1 2027, so the filing is technically allowed. But Feb 2027 to Aug 2028 is 18 months with a priority voucher, and the candidate itself calls this a priority review, which is strained. This is also the main driver of a 28% best-efficacy figure and retatrutide's market role.

least_plausible_claims.quote: About 2.5M beneficiaries fill under an obesity indication: 2.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.4B a year in gross federal spend.
least_plausible_claims.why: Arithmetic is correct, but the payer-mix claim of Medicare 17% (10.4M) is built on 2.5M obesity users plus 7.9M diabetes/CV users, and the $245 rate is applied to all obesity fills with no net-of-copay or rebate treatment. The Bridge pilot covered roughly 10% newly eligible enrollees, so a jump to 2.5M with only 70% of plans participating is asserted, not shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: One-year persistence on continuous fills has risen to about 42%, helped by cheaper pills and no injection.
least_plausible_claims.why: Persistence rose from ~35% to 42% in two years, but the mechanism is asserted. It also sits awkwardly with the stipulated high adoption, the cycling arithmetic, and the claim that most of the 2026 cohort stopped.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder society with new losers: a class-sorted body (30% top vs 15.5% bottom use, 1 in 5 vs 1 in 2 among those with obesity), coverage that follows diagnosis codes rather than need, and 440k minors on the drugs with no long-term data. The 'flatness' complaint (27% weekly muted enjoyment) is managed with weekend dose holidays, which is mild but widespread, and the epistemic picture is only partly bad since the harm is named and surveyed. Cohesion costs include 'mismatched appetite' in couples, but there is no collapse, so inequality dominates at 7 and the overall sits near 5.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visible. The oral-parity driver is realised through a 50 mg pill, the dementia label through the diabetes indication, and managed decline, employer retreat (60→44), tariffs and class stratification all trace to fields and events. mechanism: Most chains are shown (tariff → exemption → Novo price cuts; employer retreat → step-to-oral). Others are asserted: the 42% persistence rise, the 2.5M Medicare obesity users, the quick jump to ~half of pediatric obesity prescribing, and the retatrutide approval timing, which the candidate's own priority voucher narrative strains. magnitude: Population is inside the envelope (23.2 on-drug, 29 ever, income split brackets 23.2). Pediatric is stated as ≈0.6% of under-18s yet 'up from 0.6% in 2026' for children with obesity, which is confusing, and the ever-use of 29 is near the 30.2 cap. Payer mix sums to 100% of 61M, and the ~$7.4B vs ≈$3.9B CBO overrun is shown. Residual gaps: the on-drug age-band check treats weights loosely, and 10.4M Medicare users versus 2.5M + 7.9M is only just consistent.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Ocampo day-in-the-life is strong: concrete place names (Mesquite, Balch Springs, Frisco, Terrell), the Saturday skipped dose, the billboard, and the dental-office patients who show class stratification without explaining it. Supporting detail such as Netflix comedians, 'Saturday self', and bars' Friday spike gives many implied scenes and characters.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Still pro-access and pro-speed on approvals, with priority vouchers used for retatrutide's review.
least_plausible_claims.why: A priority voucher implies a review of a few months, but retatrutide was filed Feb 2027 and approved Aug 2028, about 18 months later. The world uses the voucher as colour and never explains why it did not shorten the review (mechanism).

least_plausible_claims.quote: About 33% of US households now include a user.
least_plausible_claims.why: In 2026, 11% of adults on the drug corresponded to 21–23% of households, roughly 2×. At 23.2% of adults the household share should be well above 33%, so the figure does not reconcile with the population figure and understates the food-demand base (magnitude).

least_plausible_claims.quote: The 2028 label rests on a narrower population, adults with diabetes and no dementia, using a prespecified cognitive-outcome endpoint plus pooled CVOT data.
least_plausible_claims.why: The FDA is asked to grant a dementia-risk-reduction indication on pooled cardiovascular-outcome data, after the EVOKE trials failed and with neurologists disputing the effect. No chain shows how such a thin package clears the agency in under two years (mechanism).

rationale.badness: The main harm is stratification. Use is 30% in the top income third against 15.5% in the bottom, a muscled body works as a class credential, and coverage follows diagnosis codes while use follows income. Reward blunting is now a mainstream complaint (27% weekly muted enjoyment), a third of ever-users have cycled, and 440k minors are on the drug with no long-horizon data. Offsetting this, cash pills at $149 and falling obesity keep aggregate health and flourishing from being very bad, and the harm is named and surveyed, so epistemic is middling.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visibly realised in fields and events. The 50 mg Wegovy pill meets oral parity as an existing product in a new form. Employer coverage falls to 44%, the dementia label appears in May 2028, tariffs are in the events, and the class split runs through the whole world. Safety_signal 'none' is held, since no new signals appear apart from the survey-level reward-blunting complaint. mechanism: Many chains are shown, including tariff exemptions, the step-to-oral rule, pill holidays and the Medicare spending overrun. Several changes are asserted or inconsistent: priority vouchers alongside an 18-month retatrutide review, a dementia label on a thin evidentiary package, Health Canada restricting bulk exports, persistence rising to 42% with little support, and 'as already planned' for a Part D model absent from the parent world. magnitude: On-drug 23.2%, ever-used 29%, the income thirds (average ≈23.2) and the approval timings (CagriSema, retatrutide filed Feb 2027 and approved after 12 months) all sit inside the envelope, and there is no US generic. Payer mix sums to 61M, Medicare 10.4M equals 2.5M + 7.9M, and $7.35B against CBO's ≈$3.9B/yr is shown. The pediatric 440k reconciles. Minor gaps remain: household incidence of 33% is too low, and the '10 pp of ever-users' wording is sloppy.
rationale.generativity: Denise Ocampo's day in Mesquite contains the skipped Saturday dose, the $149 bottle, the Frisco patient and Mr. Lyle from Terrell, the 'memory one' Rybelsus and the MADE HERE billboard. The world also carries texture such as the Plano/Kaufman contrast, the 'Saturday self', the Friday spike and dating profiles listing the drug. Many scenes are implied and the prose shows rather than explains.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The 2028 label rests on a narrower population, adults with diabetes and no dementia, using a prespecified cognitive-outcome endpoint plus pooled CVOT data.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: The driver only stipulates a dementia indication. The candidate invents an evidentiary basis (pooled CVOT data plus an unnamed trial endpoint) that FDA would be unlikely to accept for a dementia-risk claim, especially after EVOKE failed. No trial that supplies the endpoint is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Orforglipron's short half-life makes 1–3 day holidays effective.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: Orforglipron's half-life is roughly 1–2 days, not clearly short enough for reward-blunting to lift within 1–3 days. The whole 'Friday spike' and 'Saturday self' culture rests on this asserted pharmacology, with no supporting data.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicaid: about 30 states cover obesity at the $245 reference rate, ≈6.1M users.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: The 2026 world only says Medicaid was 'expected to follow', and states were cutting GLP-1 obesity coverage under budget pressure. Reaching 30 states and 6.1M users (about $17.9B a year at $245) is aggressive and given without a state-budget mechanism.

rationale.badness: The main harm is stratification. Use is 30% in the top income third against 15.5% in the bottom, coverage follows diagnosis codes while use follows income, and lean muscled bodies work as a class credential. Weekly muted enjoyment in 27% of users, 440k minors on the drugs with no long-horizon data, and cycling by a third of ever-users add real but diffuse harm. Obesity falls, pills are cheap, and the safety ledger shows no new signal, so this is a harder society with new losers rather than a structural catastrophe.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised and traceable: adoption 23.2%, managed price decline to $149–349, employer coverage down to 44%, a dementia label in May 2028, no new safety signal, a 50 mg pill for oral parity, Section 232 tariffs, class stratification, no new federal programme, and flatness as a mainstream complaint. mechanism: Most chains are shown, notably coverage retreating to diagnosis codes, tariff exemptions bought with US capacity, and holidays driving the Friday spike. Several links are asserted, namely the dementia evidence basis, the orforglipron half-life claim (claim 2), the speed of the head-to-head trial, and Medicaid expansion (claim 3). magnitude: Current use of 23.2% and ever-use of 29% sit inside the envelope. The income thirds average to the national figure, the age bands compute to 23.2, the payer mix sums to 61M, and Medicare ($7.4B) and the pediatric 440k reconcile. The CagriSema and retatrutide approval timings are allowed. Minor gaps: the 8.5 pp of current users who restarted implies a restart rate above the 2026 figures, and the Medicaid count is aggressive.
rationale.generativity: The prose has a fully drawn day. Denise in Mesquite skips Saturday's pill for the quinceañera, the front-desk contrast between the Frisco woman and Mr. Lyle, the billboard 'MADE HERE. PRICED FOR YOU.', and her mother calling Rybelsus 'the memory one'. The world fields add Plano versus Kaufman County, dating profiles listing medication, and the 'Saturday self'. Many scenes and characters are implied.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Retatrutide's BLA was filed Feb 2027 and approved Aug 2028 (more than 12 months after filing).
least_plausible_claims.why: Starting world says the BLA is planned ~Q1 2027, so the filing is technically allowed. But Feb 2027 to Aug 2028 is 18 months with a priority voucher, and the candidate itself calls this a priority review, which is strained. This is also the main driver of a 28% best-efficacy figure and retatrutide's market role.

least_plausible_claims.quote: About 2.5M beneficiaries fill under an obesity indication: 2.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.4B a year in gross federal spend.
least_plausible_claims.why: Arithmetic is correct, but the payer-mix claim of Medicare 17% (10.4M) is built on 2.5M obesity users plus 7.9M diabetes/CV users, and the $245 rate is applied to all obesity fills with no net-of-copay or rebate treatment. The Bridge pilot covered roughly 10% newly eligible enrollees, so a jump to 2.5M with only 70% of plans participating is asserted, not shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: One-year persistence on continuous fills has risen to about 42%, helped by cheaper pills and no injection.
least_plausible_claims.why: Persistence rose from ~35% to 42% in two years, but the mechanism is asserted. It also sits awkwardly with the stipulated high adoption, the cycling arithmetic, and the claim that most of the 2026 cohort stopped.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder society with new losers: a class-sorted body (30% top vs 15.5% bottom use, 1 in 5 vs 1 in 2 among those with obesity), coverage that follows diagnosis codes rather than need, and 440k minors on the drugs with no long-term data. The 'flatness' complaint (27% weekly muted enjoyment) is managed with weekend dose holidays, which is mild but widespread, and the epistemic picture is only partly bad since the harm is named and surveyed. Cohesion costs include 'mismatched appetite' in couples, but there is no collapse, so inequality dominates at 7 and the overall sits near 5.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visible. The oral-parity driver is realised through a 50 mg pill, the dementia label through the diabetes indication, and managed decline, employer retreat (60→44), tariffs and class stratification all trace to fields and events. mechanism: Most chains are shown (tariff → exemption → Novo price cuts; employer retreat → step-to-oral). Others are asserted: the 42% persistence rise, the 2.5M Medicare obesity users, the quick jump to ~half of pediatric obesity prescribing, and the retatrutide approval timing, which the candidate's own priority voucher narrative strains. magnitude: Population is inside the envelope (23.2 on-drug, 29 ever, income split brackets 23.2). Pediatric is stated as ≈0.6% of under-18s yet 'up from 0.6% in 2026' for children with obesity, which is confusing, and the ever-use of 29 is near the 30.2 cap. Payer mix sums to 100% of 61M, and the ~$7.4B vs ≈$3.9B CBO overrun is shown. Residual gaps: the on-drug age-band check treats weights loosely, and 10.4M Medicare users versus 2.5M + 7.9M is only just consistent.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Ocampo day-in-the-life is strong: concrete place names (Mesquite, Balch Springs, Frisco, Terrell), the Saturday skipped dose, the billboard, and the dental-office patients who show class stratification without explaining it. Supporting detail such as Netflix comedians, 'Saturday self', and bars' Friday spike gives many implied scenes and characters.
